key_insight: In SMAW of AISI/SAE 1020 steel, quenching medium dominates joint performance far more than groove angle, and the best overall ranking is consistent across multiple decision methods.
engineering_relevance: For weld design and post-weld heat treatment, choosing the cooling medium matters most for balancing strength, toughness, and strain-hardening behavior.
method: Analyzed 55–60° single-V groove welds under three quenching media: air, water, and palm oil
Used effect-share analysis, machine-learning surrogates, and functional ANOVA on recovered stress–strain data
Applied four multi-criteria ranking methods: GRA, TOPSIS, desirability, and entropy-weighted GRA
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quenching medium explains about 70.3–94.6% of response effects, and all four ranking schemes produced the same order; Gaussian-process uncertainty on toughness was about ±9%.
watch_item: The conclusions are specific to the tested groove-angle range, steel grade, and cooling conditions, so they should not be generalized without validation on other weld setups.
paper_title: Groove angle and quenching medium in shielded metal arc welding of mild steel: Multi-criteria decision analysis, machine learning and energy absorption
